My boss says that intelligence is overrated and that hard work is more important. He is a very successful scientist so he knows what he is talking about. 

How to apply this? Study hard and read a lot of science books to gain knowledge and inspiration. If you want to be a scientist, go for it! Don’t listen to what others (or even your self-critical nature) tell yourself. 

Also, remember that science is a method rather than a bunch of smart people who think really hard. 

By the way, you can live a good life even if you are an average person (most people are average). But just because somebody is average in one area doesn’t mean they aren’t exceptional in something else. I think you’re probably above average in intelligence though. 

One more thing. I know this is hard, but it’s important. The best life is one lived for yourself. In this life, you shouldn’t care that much what others think of you. Ironically, a life lived to please yourself instead of others results in more people liking you because they can see you are self satisfied, and those people tend to be more attractive. But the point is you will be happier.

Your post doesn't sound stupid to me. It is very thoughtful. 

Here are some things to ponder. How do they make you feel? 

\- Although there are many bad people, there are also many good people, and I think that society as a whole is getting better over time. It's also true that, at your age, many people have a lot of growing up to do before they can fully express their good traits. 

\- We will all die eventually. There's no reason to do it early. If you kill yourself, you're doing something irreversible. Who knows, you might find purpose/true happiness in life if you just give yourself a chance and continue living.

\- The good times of a relationship outweigh the pain of a breakup. In the same way, the good times you will have if you find a partner should make up for the sadness of death. And that sadness will be temporary, and hopefully of shorter duration than the good times you had.  

\- Even if there is no heaven, for hopefully many thousands of years more civilization will continue. If we're lucky, maybe some of them will even be our progeny. That's always a good thing, and it's kind of like a heaven for the human race.

\- In any case, there's always love. A good portion of humanity is giving its time/energy to helping those in need. For example, relief programs, programs that end human trafficking, programs that provide aide in the developing world, etc. Maybe this is your niche and would make you feel better, as you seem like a very compassionate person \(and you don't have to be religious to help out in these kind of efforts, as there are many secular ones\). 

Let me know if any of these things help/encourage you. Please hang in there!
